open_obligations: Check the authors' own limitation that inserted bugs differ in distribution from natural LLM errors.
Note the domain change from summarisation to code, where bugs are more objectively checkable.
Check whether reference bugs reduce over-trust in critiques or only make critique-bug inclusion measurable.
in.other_title: Adversarial tampering: humans insert subtle bugs that an LLM critic misses
in.rationale: Saunders et al. state their summarisation task has no objective way to validate answers or critiques and that labelers may over-trust critiques. McAleese et al. have contractors insert subtle bugs into model-written code, verified to be missed by a critic at least once, and use these tamper descriptions as reference bugs for rating critiques; they also report critics trained without tampering severely underperform, but inserted bugs differ from natural errors.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how to obtain reference flaws for evaluating critiques when the base task lacks objective ground truth, for LLM critiques of code

text: The authors state their base task has no robust or objective way to validate answers or critiques: labelers may misevaluate answers by over-trusting model summaries or making mistakes, some assisted critiques were nitpicky, agreement on critique and answer comparisons was only about 75%, and misleading critiques of good outputs may be indistinguishable from good critiques of poor outputs. They also say they do not address how to measure ground truth, relying on labelers who will be increasingly unreliable on harder tasks.
title: No ground truth for topic-based summarization; labelers may over-trust model critiques
